proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current question advertises the sharp radial exponent as an unconditional full-class confidence diameter, although the frozen core proves only the scalar finite-type full-class exponent and leaves the sharper arbitrary-map coercivity in oeq:full-incompressible-rigidity unresolved. The replacement states the proved fixed-order diameter and makes the sharper target explicitly conditional on that open result.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This installs the directed maximality correction, adds the newly used dimension symbol and full-rigidity dependency, and synchronizes the open-obligation record with the proved conservative fixed-order diameter.

proposed.justification: Unknown critical order is empirically unavoidable, but honest adaptation across nonregular inverse exponents may require an explicit testing margin.
proposed.gap: Bull and Nickl characterize smoothness adaptation for ordinary \(L^2\) density sets, not adaptation across causal inverse orders or proximity to a nonidentified plateau.
proposed.consumer: The result would tell practitioners when the critical order can be learned from data, when the proved conservative fixed-order representing-model diameter is attainable adaptively, and when a worst-order radius is unavoidable.

obligation.what_is_open: A numerical separation functional, an honest adaptive test over critical orders, and a matching impossibility theorem below its testing boundary.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen adaptation handle does not define a topology or numerical distance to lower-order and plateau classes, and no minimax testing modulus for those boundaries has been proved. The sharper fixed-order diameter additionally depends on the unresolved full incompressible-rigidity question.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-order spectral law ball, corrected coverage theorem, and proved scalar finite-type modulus yield honest conservative fixed-order representing-model diameters, but these facts do not construct a test of critical order or identify its sharp separation boundary.
obligation.partial_result: For each fixed known \(m\), the frozen confidence theorem gives an honest quotient-valued set with representing-model diameter of order \(\rho_N^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\). The sharper order \(\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) would follow only after an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\). No distance to the union of lower-order classes or to the closure of plateau profiles is defined, so neither an adaptive testing rule nor a matching below-boundary impossibility theorem is determined by the frozen construction.

prose_updates.tldr: Complete paired interventions yield a synthetic product law and ratio residuals. For the full bounded finite-type class, the proved inverse-modulus result is the bracket \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\); the matching full-class upper exponent remains open in \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\). The radial subclass is sharp at \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). In the primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse case, this means a full-class \(3/4\) lower exponent versus a \(1/3\) upper exponent, with a sharp radial exponent \(3/4\). Zero-law componentwise circular recovery follows from the direct torus identification argument, not from a converse characterization of \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\). The certified Fourier estimator and the representing-model diameter of the quotient-valued confidence set inherit the conservative exponent, giving the primary rate \(N^{-1/12}\).

project_justification.gap: CauCA and score-based causal representation learning establish componentwise exact identification under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy, but they do not provide a symmetric two-law aligned discrepancy for approximate recovery or quantify isolated critical zeros. Quantitative Morse perturbation results requiring higher smoothness do not justify the primary \(C^2\) case, and near-isometry robustness controls a different primitive defect.
project_justification.niche: Circular latent coordinates permit a directly stated \(C^2\) Morse class and a separate finite-type hierarchy with exact uniform margins and attained worst order. Complete intervention laws add a determinant channel, while the symmetric two-law aligned discrepancy removes dependence on which competing model is declared the reference.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the synthetic product reduction, a direct zero-law torus identification result, the localized full-class lower obstruction, the conservative scalar-rigidity upper bound, the exact radial frontier, and the environment-by-environment two-node Morse audit. It also gives certified Fourier recovery and a quotient-valued confidence set whose representing-model diameter has the conservative rate, while isolating full-class incompressible rigidity as the step needed to close the exponent gap.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Positive truncated Fourier density estimation uses the vanishing floor \(\eta_N=N^{-1}\) and corrected normalization, followed by a certified finite minimum-distance fit; no derivative of an estimated density is required. The true observed densities retain the uniform lower bound \(c_0K^{-n}\). The log-free law radius \(\rho_N=N^{-s_{\mathrm{obs}}/(2s_{\mathrm{obs}}+n)}\) is propagated through the proved exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\), which yields \(N^{-1/12}\) in the primary case.

prose_updates.related_work: Liang et al. establish exact CauCA recovery under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy and exhibit determinant-one rotations on common plateaus. Varıcı et al. derive componentwise and graph recovery from exact sparse score changes under paired node interventions. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) proves the present zero-law torus conclusion directly and uses those papers only to compare assumptions and conclusion types. Neither comparator supplies a nonzero-error modulus. Buchholz and Schölkopf quantify near-isometric representation learning through a different primitive defect. Khesin et al. motivate the volume-preserving kernel, while Dacorogna--Moser and Teixeira provide prescribed-Jacobian and localized volume-correction context. Milnor supports the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse condition. Compact-manifold density-band results and Bull--Nickl's adaptive \(L^2\)-set theory support the sampling rung, but the propagation exponent here comes from the proved scalar finite-type rigidity lemma.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The general contribution is a full-class bracket: lower exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) and upper exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\). The radial restricted supremum has the sharp exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\). For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), the full bracket is \(c\varepsilon^{3/4}\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}\), the radial rate is exactly of order \(\varepsilon^{3/4}\), and the certified estimator and representing-model confidence-set diameter have rate \(N^{-1/12}\). The primary class uses separated critical points and the direct Hessian bound \(|r_i''(z)|\geq a_0\), without invoking a higher-smoothness quantitative-Morse theorem. Plateaus, coalescing critical points, critical submanifolds, vector-valued contrast curves, unknown-order adaptation, and the matching full-class upper bound remain outside the proved claim.

statement_notes.justification: A law-to-representation modulus and a representing-model confidence-set diameter require a symmetric two-law aligned discrepancy rather than a loss directed from one selected model.

statement_notes.consumer: Every lower bound, upper modulus, estimator guarantee, and representing-model confidence-set diameter uses the same symmetric aligned discrepancy.
